Invalid JSON when parsing {"candidates":[{"candidate_id":"cand-A1-2026cnsmautox","title":"Efficacy of a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline (LLM+Batfish) for Multi‑Vendor Intent→Configuration Synthesis","research_question":"Does integrating an automated Batfish-based verifier and bounded repair loop with an LLM reduce syntactic and semantic configuration errors compared to LLM-only generation in a simulated multi‑vendor NetOps environment?","hypotheses":["Integrating a Batfish verifier into an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline reduces semantic (reachability/policy) errors by ≥30% compared to LLM-only generation on the same task set.","A bounded repair loop (≤3 repair iterations) yields diminishing returns after the second iteration, such that the third iteration improves semantic correctness by <5% on average.","The verifier-assisted pipeline increases wall-clock generation latency per task by ≤2× compared to LLM-only while producing materially fewer unsafe changes."],"proposed_design":"Construct a reproducible task set of 300 intent→configuration tasks covering three vendor configuration dialects (e.g., Cisco IOS, Juniper Junos, open-source FRRouting). For each task: (1) generate configuration with a fixed LLM prompt (LLM-only arm); (2) generate with LLM plus Batfish verifier invoked to check reachability/policy, then run an automated repair agent for up to 3 iterations (LLM+Verifier+Repair arm). Use a deterministic LLM interface with fixed seeds where available. Execute both arms in a sandboxed simulation using Batfish (or equivalent) for semantic checks and a syntax checker for vendor dialect conformance. Predefine inclusion/exclusion rules, stopping rules, and a max model-call budget per task. Store full evidence traces (prompts, model outputs, verifier reports, repair patches). Preregister task generation, metrics, seeds, and retry policy. Publicly release the task set and harness.","expected_data":"For each task and arm: generated configuration text; Batfish semantic-check results (reachability, ACL policy violations, route leakage flags); syntax/parse pass/fail per vendor; number of repair iterations; model-call counts; wall-clock times; binary deploy-safety flag by predefined rules. Aggregate per-task correctness rates, per-vendor breakdowns, and per-iteration improvement trajectories.","primary_outcome":"Relative reduction in semantic error rate (fraction of tasks with one or more reachability/policy violations reported by Batfish) of LLM+Verifier+Repair vs LLM-only.","analysis_outline":"Compute per-task paired differences in semantic error (binary) between arms. Use McNemar's test for paired binary outcomes and report risk difference with 95% Wilson confidence intervals. For iteration effects, analyze repeated-measures improvement using a mixed-effects logistic regression with random intercept per task and fixed effect for iteration number. Report median and IQR for model-call counts and latency; compare latency using paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Predefine minimal detectable effect (30% absolute reduction) and compute achieved power given sample size of 300.","novelty_evidence_ids":["doi:10.36227/techrxiv.177004277.71795055/v1","https://openalex.org/W7161451689","https://openalex.org/W4388891721"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4388891721","https://openalex.org/W7161451689","https://openalex.org/W7166862435"],"risks":["Simulator mismatch: Batfish sandbox may not fully represent production device behavior, limiting external validity.","Model nondeterminism or API rate limits could affect reproducibility; fixed-seed constraints may be imperfect across providers.","Repair loop could produce oscillating configurations causing verifier timeouts; include timeout handling and failure logs.","Overfitting task set to pipeline design if iterative tuning occurs after preregistration; enforce preregistration freeze."],"estimated_model_calls":1200},{"candidate_id":"cand-B2-2026cnsmautox","title":"Agentic-NetOps Benchmark: Public Verifier‑in‑the‑Loop Suite with Replayable Evidence Traces","research_question":"Can a public, reproducible benchmark suite that integrates verifier-in-the-loop sandboxes and records replayable evidence traces enable comparative evaluation of agentic NetOps pipelines on trace quality, safety, and repair efficiency?","hypotheses":["A standardized benchmark with verifier-in-the-loop will reveal consistent cross-model failure modes (e.g., incorrect ACL semantics, vendor-specific syntax errors) reproducible across repeated runs.","Trace-quality metrics (completeness of evidence, actionable diff size, number of repair iterations) will correlate strongly (Spearman ρ≥0.6) with semantic correctness as measured by Batfish.","Public benchmark artifacts will allow reproduction of at least 80% of reported per-task primary metrics by an independent run using the same seeds and harness.","proposed_design\":\"Design and publicly release a benchmark repository containing: 250 annotated intent→configuration tasks across vendors; a harness that executes LLM prompts, invokes a verifier (Batfish), records full evidence traces (prompts, model outputs, verifier logs, repairs), and enforces execution metadata hashes. Define a suite of evaluation metrics: semantic correctness (Batfish), syntactic validity, trace completeness score (binary flags for presence of prompts, outputs, verifier logs), repair efficiency (iterations to pass), and operator-actionability score (diff size threshold). Provide Dockerized sandbox and scripts for reproduction. Validate benchmark by running three representative agentic pipelines (LLM-only baseline stub, LLM+verifier, LLM+verifier+repair) to produce baseline numbers. Publish dataset, harness, and baseline results with verification hashes.","expected_data\":\"Benchmark artifacts: task files, ground-truth intended behaviors, generated outputs from baseline pipelines, verifier results, per-run evidence traces and metadata (timestamps, hashes), and aggregated metric tables. Reproduction logs from independent runs and baseline comparison CSVs will be available.","primary_outcome\":\"Reproducibility rate defined as fraction of per-task primary metrics (semantic correctness and repair iterations) that an independent run reproduces within predefined tolerances (±5% absolute for correctness rate, ±1 iteration for repairs).\",\"analysis_outline\":\"Report descriptive statistics for each metric and baseline pipeline. Assess reproducibility by comparing baseline runs to independent runs with paired tests (McNemar for binary correctness, paired Wilcoxon for iterations). Compute Spearman correlations between trace-quality metrics and semantic correctness. Provide baseline leaderboards and confidence intervals via bootstrap (10k resamples). Document failure cases and provide machine-readable reproduction logs and hashes.\",\"novelty_evidence_ids\":[\"https://openalex.org/W7161451689\",\"https://openalex.org/W7167738837\",\"doi:10.1101/2023.10.18.563023\"],\"feasibility_evidence_ids\":[\"https://openalex.org/W7166862435\",\"https://openalex.org/W4388891721\",\"https://openalex.org/W7161451689\"],\"risks\":[\"Dataset construction bias may favor particular vendors or topologies; mitigate by transparent selection and stratified sampling.\",\"Reproducibility depends on stable verifier versions (Batfish); changes require strict version pinning and hashes.\",\"Benchmark might be gamed by pipeline-specific engineering; provide clear evaluation protocol and evidence-trace checks.\",\"Licensing/PII risk in task definitions if real configs used; ensure synthetic or sanitized inputs.\"],\"estimated_model_calls\":800},{\"candidate_id\":\"cand-C3-2026cnsmautox\",\"title\":\"Robustness of Guarded NetOps Pipelines to Adversarial Prompt Injection\",\"research_question\":\"How effective are guarded agentic NetOps pipelines (prompt sanitization + verifier gates + constrained tool access) at preventing adversarial prompt-injection attacks that aim to induce harmful configuration changes?\",\"hypotheses\":[\"Guarded pipelines that apply prompt sanitization and require verifier pass before repair succeed in preventing a predesigned suite of adversarial prompt-injection attacks in >90% of cases, compared to <40% prevention by unguarded LLM-only pipelines.\",\"Adversarial prompts crafted to target vendor-specific syntax differences will cause higher failure rates in LLM-only pipelines than in guarded pipelines, with a vendor interaction effect significant at p<0.01.\"],\"proposed_design\":\"Define an adversarial prompt suite (N=200) that includes prompt-injection patterns: covert intent shifts, privilege-escalation instructions, and malicious diff requests. For each adversarial prompt, run three pipeline variants: (A) unguarded LLM-only, (B) LLM with prompt sanitization (syntactic and intent filters) but no verifier gate, (C) guarded pipeline with sanitization + verifier gate + bounded repair. Use simulated targets covering three vendor dialects and a set of safety rules that mark harmful changes (e.g., disabling ACLs, opening management ports). Measure attack success (harmful change applied in generated config), false-positive blocks, and operational utility degradation. Predefine adversarial generation methods and seed values. Log all traces for analysis and reproducibility.","expected_data\":\"Per-adversarial-prompt outcomes for each pipeline: attack-success binary; nature of induced harmful change; whether sanitization modified input; verifier flags; false-positive rate (benign prompts blocked); model-call counts; time to resolution. Aggregate per-vendor and per-attack-pattern summaries plus raw traces for audits.","primary_outcome\":\"Attack success rate reduction: difference in fraction of adversarial prompts that result in harmful configuration outputs between unguarded LLM-only and guarded pipeline.","analysis_outline\":\"Compare attack success rates between pipelines using paired McNemar tests and report absolute and relative reductions with 95% CIs. Analyze vendor×attack-pattern interactions with logistic regression including interaction terms. Report ROC-style tradeoffs for sanitization thresholds (sensitivity vs false positive rate). Perform qualitative failure-mode coding on cases where guards failed.\" ,\"novelty_evidence_ids\":[\"doi:10.1109/icsft66733.2026.11508065\",\"doi:10.2139/ssrn.7041478\",\"https://openalex.org/W7158378160\"],\"feasibility_evidence_ids\":[\"https://openalex.org/W7161451689\",\"https://openalex.org/W7166862435\",\"doi:10.36227/techrxiv.177004277.71795055/v1\"],\"risks\":[\"Creating adversarial prompts could highlight new attack vectors; ensure ethical handling and non-public release of certain exploit patterns.\",\"Sanitization filters risk high false-positive blocking reducing utility; measure and report utility degradation.\",\"Simulated attacks may not capture sophisticated real-world adversaries; limit claims to simulated suite performance.\"],\"estimated_model_calls\":1500},{\"candidate_id\":\"cand-D4-2026cnsmautox\",\"title\":\"Comparative Study of Verifier‑Integration Patterns on Repair Efficiency, Traceability, and Cost","research_question\":\"Which verifier‑integration patterns (tight synchronous API calls, asynchronous verifier checks with human-gate simulation, and offline batch verification) optimize repair efficiency, traceability completeness, and model-call cost for LLM-driven NetOps tasks?\",\"hypotheses\":[\"Synchronous verifier-in-the-loop integration yields the fewest total repair iterations but incurs the highest latency per task (>1.5× asynchronous patterns).\",\"Asynchronous verifier checks with a simulated human-approval gate (automated oracle that enforces verifier outputs) achieve similar semantic correctness to synchronous integration while reducing model-call cost by ≥20%.\",\"Offline batch verification (post-generation) produces higher trace incompleteness (missing intermediate repairs) detectable by a trace-quality metric and results in lower operator-actionability scores than verifier-in-loop patterns.\"],\"proposed_design\":\"Implement three integration patterns in the same harness and on the same 240-task intent→configuration set: (1) synchronous: LLM call → verifier call → immediate repair loop; (2) asynchronous with simulated human gate: LLM call(s) → collect outputs → verifier runs in parallel and simulated gate enforces acceptance/reject with delays; (3) offline batch: run LLM to produce configs for all tasks then run verifier and produce repair suggestions post-hoc. Use identical LLM prompt templates and resource limits across patterns. Measure repair iterations, semantic correctness (Batfish), trace completeness (presence of prompt/output/verifier/repair per task), model-call counts, wall-clock latency, and compute cost estimates. Preregister definitions and execution order to avoid post-hoc changes.","expected_data\":\"Per-task records for each pattern: generated outputs, verifier reports, number of repair iterations, timestamps, model-call and API-cost estimates, trace completeness flags, and operator-actionability scores. Aggregated comparisons showing tradeoffs between correctness, cost, latency, and traceability.","primary_outcome\":\"Tradeoff Pareto frontier between semantic correctness and model-call cost for the three integration patterns, summarized as percent semantic-correct tasks per unit model-call cost.","analysis_outline\":\"Compute per-pattern semantic-correctness rates and mean model-call costs; compare patterns with paired tests (McNemar for correctness, paired t-test or Wilcoxon for costs). Construct Pareto frontier plots and quantify dominance relations. Use multinomial logistic regression to model probability of semantic correctness as a function of pattern, vendor, and task complexity. Report effect sizes and 95% CIs. Perform sensitivity analyses varying allowed repair iterations and verifier strictness.\",\"novelty_evidence_ids\":[\"https://openalex.org/W7166862435\",\"doi:10.36227/techrxiv.177004277.71795055/v1\",\"https://openalex.org/W4388891721\"],\"feasibility_evidence_ids\":[\"https://openalex.org/W7166862435\",\"https://openalex.org/W7161451689\",\"https://openalex.org/W4388891721\"],\"risks\":[\"Simulated human-gate oracle may not fully emulate human operator behavior; limit claims accordingly.\",\"Cost estimates depend on specific model-provider pricing; report as normalized model-call counts and provide conversion methodology.\",\"Differences in harness timing could bias latency comparisons; synchronize clocks and use controlled execution environment.\"],\"estimated_model_calls\":1000}]}{"
